look_here_first: Start with the big asymmetric leaf and the spring samara: American elm has relatively large double-serrate leaves with a strongly uneven base, then a flat oval samara with a ciliate margin and a deep apical notch.

project_inclusion.range_basis: 24-county boundary audit 2026-10-14: Hays, Travis qualify; Bell out-of-zone and excluded from PASS. Previous evidence preserved in range_audit; third approved county pending.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Bell and Travis are herbarium collection records interpreted within a source-confirmed native Texas range; planted street-tree records are not used.

range_audit.confidence: high for county boundary/count correction; prior locality evidence not independently reexamined
range_audit.reason: Old PASS required 3 approved counties, but only 2 in stored evidence are inside zone. Not an assertion that other local wild populations are absent.
range_audit.original_range_basis: Kew/POWO accepts Ulmus americana and lists Texas in its native range. Hays County — the project Hays County native-source list includes U. americana. Bell County — USDA ARS Biocollections preserves multiple 2014 specimens collected at the Little River near Little River-Academy. Travis County — USDA ARS Biocollections preserves a 2014 U. americana specimen from Redbud Island, Austin.

best_field_traits: large deciduous elm, often developing a vase-shaped crown
leaves mostly >7 cm, ovate to elliptic with strongly oblique base
lower leaf surface glabrous to pubescent, often with tufts in vein axils
flowers before leaf-out in spring on slender pedicels
oval spring samara with seed near center, ciliate margin, and a deep apical notch
morphology_keys.elm_training: Read leaf texture/asymmetry together with twig wings, bark, reproductive season and samara characters.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Ulmus rubra: Slippery elm has red-tomentose bud-scale margins, much rougher thick leaves, and a samara pubescent on the body rather than a ciliate margin. Ulmus alata: Winged elm has smaller leaves and conspicuous regular corky wings on branches; American elm lacks those wings. Ulmus crassifolia: Cedar elm has much smaller rough leaves and reproduces in fall rather than spring.
